AfterAddedToRoom.maps_to: PunchConstruct.__init__ (punch_construct.py:29-40) for the Artifact; _PunchOffEncounter.create_monsters (events/punch_off.py:22-30) for the HP reduction
AfterAddedToRoom.issue: RE-OPENED 2026-07-28. Three clauses, three different answers, and only one of them is closed. CLAUSE 2a (WHICH FIELD) IS CLOSED: _PunchOffEncounter.create_monsters (events/punch_off.py:26-33) is now `m.hp = max(1, m.hp - reduction)` with max_hp left at PunchConstruct's flat 55 (punch_construct.py:26-27), matching PunchConstruct.cs:75-78's `SetCurrentHpInternal(Math.Max(1, Creature.CurrentHp - StartingHpReduction))`, which touches MaxHp not at all; `py audit/tools/monster_probes_b03.py punchoff-hp` reports hp=53 max_hp=55 and hp=49 max_hp=55. The NextInt(2, 10) RANGE and the first construct's StartsWithFastPunch flag were already correct. CLAUSE 1 (ArtifactPower 1, PunchConstruct.cs:74, applied from punch_construct.py:39-40 rather than from an add-to-room phase) remains SHARED-FINDINGS section 2's pool-wide deliberate divergence -- see this entry's rationale. CLAUSE 2b IS STILL A GAP, and it is why this entry cannot read 'no live gap': the two reductions are drawn off the WRONG STREAM and, on the parity path, then erased. events/punch_off.py:26 accepts a `selection_rng` argument and IGNORES it, rolling `rng.randint(2, 9)` on the shared combat random.Random at :30, where PunchOffEventEncounter.cs:17,:19 roll `base.Rng.NextInt(2, 10)` twice on the per-encounter EncounterModel Rng (EncounterModel.cs:259-270). The plumbing is already in place and five sibling encounters use it (monsters/glory/scroll_of_biting.py:105-108, monsters/underdocks/corpse_slug.py:84, monsters/overgrowth/slithering_strangler.py:74, monsters/hive/decimillipede.py:156, monsters/overgrowth/slimes.py:190); run.py:1299-1303 builds the stream and combat.py:135-136 passes it into create_monsters, and punch_off is reached through PunchOff.canonical_encounter. Consequences: 0 draws on the per-encounter stream where the game takes 2, 2 extra draws on the shared rng, different construct HP for a given run seed and floor -- and on the parity path the reduction is wiped outright, because create_monsters runs BEFORE CombatState._assign_parity_monster_hp, whose _roll_parity_hp does `creature.hp = creature.max_hp = hp` (combat.py:263), and PregeneratedEncounter.create_monsters does the same at events/_combat_layout.py:73-74. audit/records/event/punch_off.json carries this as two `gap` entries (guard EV-3 and the StartingHpReduction guard, both re-derived 2026-07-28), so binding rule 3 requires the same verdict here rather than a record that reports no gap. THE CORRECT HOME for the reduction is Monster.adjust_hp_after_added -- the sim's port of AfterAddedToRoom, run at combat.py:277-278 AFTER the Niche max-HP roll, exactly where PunchConstruct.cs:70-79 sits. WAS (clause 2a): the reduction was applied to max_hp and hp clamped to it, so a construct the game shows at 46/55 the sim showed at 46/46. Rule 7: sts2_rl/combat.py, sts2_rl/run.py, sts2_rl/events/_combat_layout.py, src/Core/Models/EncounterModel.cs and the five sibling monster modules are cited without being hashed by this record.
AfterAddedToRoom.rationale: The hook has two clauses and they get different answers. CLAUSE 1, ArtifactPower 1 (PunchConstruct.cs:74 -> punch_construct.py:40): deliberate-divergence by SHARED-FINDINGS section 2, whose three clauses all hold - the amount is the literal 1, the power is self-applied with no card, and the initial state is a MoveState (READY_MOVE, or FAST_PUNCH_MOVE under StartsWithFastPunch), so monster_state_machine step 30's sticky no-op means the first roll reads nothing. RULE 7 NOTE: that shared rationale cites four relic files and powers.py which this record does not hash. CLAUSE 2, StartingHpReduction: clause 2a (which HP field the reduction lands on) is closed; clause 2b (the roll is taken off the shared rng rather than the per-encounter Rng, and is erased outright on the parity path) is the gap above. EXECUTED PRE-FIX (kept as the record of what the divergence WAS -- the same probe now reports max_hp=55 for both, see the issue): `py audit/tools/monster_probes_b03.py punchoff-hp` on a real Punch-Off CombatState (seed 4) gave 'sim punch-off construct 0: hp=53 max_hp=53 initial_move=FAST_PUNCH_MOVE' and 'sim punch-off construct 1: hp=49 max_hp=49 initial_move=READY_MOVE', against a game MaxHp of 55 for both. LIVE under rule 6, both sides reachable on ported content: the same probe prints 'punch_off in the sim's Underdocks event pool: True | registered class: <class sts2_rl.events.punch_off.PunchOff>' (events/__init__.py:73-76 lists it in UNDERDOCKS_EVENTS), the encounter is PunchOffEventEncounter's port and the reduction fires unconditionally for BOTH constructs - PunchOffEventEncounter.cs:17,19 roll Rng.NextInt(2, 10), i.e. 2..9, never 0, and events/punch_off.py:26 rolls the matching randint(2, 9), so `StartingHpReduction > 0` is always true. The gap needs no relic, no potion and no player choice beyond taking the fight. Note the range and the first-construct StartsWithFastPunch flag are both ported CORRECTLY - what is wrong today is the STREAM the two rolls come off, not the range; the field they land on was fixed 2026-07-28.

guards.rationale: SHARED-FINDINGS section 7 asks whether this unit makes the dormant SetMaxAndCurrentHp finding live. It does not: PunchConstruct.cs:77 calls SetCurrentHpInternal, which is the game's own raw current-HP setter for exactly this purpose, so a sim assignment that skips the hooks is faithful to the source here. The divergence recorded on AfterAddedToRoom is about WHICH FIELD is written, not about the hooks the write skips.
